EXPLAINER: Who gets to form Israel's next government? Finishing first does not decide it.

As Tuesday's vote approaches, here is how coalition-building works under Israeli law:

• The Central Elections Committee publishes official results within eight days of the vote, so by 4 November.
• President Isaac Herzog then consults with representatives of every faction elected to the Knesset. Each faction tells him who it recommends for prime minister.
• The President gives the mandate to the Knesset member he judges to have the best chance of forming a government. This is not automatically the leader of the largest party.
• That nominee has 28 days to build a coalition, and the President can extend this by up to 14 days. A new government needs the confidence of a majority of the 120-seat Knesset, which is 61 seats.
• If the nominee fails, the President can give the mandate to another Knesset member. If that also fails, a majority of Knesset members can back a candidate. If no one succeeds, Israel goes to new elections.

In most final polls, neither the Netanyahu-led bloc nor the opposition bloc reaches 61 seats. That means the recommendations factions make to the President, and possibly lengthy negotiations, could matter more than which party finishes first.

Direct Polls, which polls for i24NEWS, has been widely cited as the most accurate pollster of 2022, a point JI also noted in its 22 Oct analysis. The firm's own account adds some detail:

• Direct Polls' final 2022 number had Likud at 34. Likud won 32, so it overestimated by 2.
• The mainstream final polls (26-28 Oct 2022) had Likud at 30-31, so they underestimated by 1-2. Those misses all ran in the same direction, toward under-counting the right.

What it means for 2026: Of 41 polls with fieldwork from 27 Sept to 22 Oct, Yashar led in 25, Likud in 14 and 2 were ties. All 14 Likud leads came from Channel 14 or i24NEWS. Mainstream pollsters say they've adjusted their weighting for past vote and religiosity since 2022.

EXPLAINER: How the 3.25% threshold works in Israel's Knesset election

• A list needs at least 3.25% of valid votes to win any seats. In practice that means at least four of the Knesset's 120 seats.
• Votes for a list that falls short are lost. The remaining seats are then shared among the lists that cross the threshold, in proportion to their vote, which slightly raises every winning party's share.
• Lists can sign surplus-vote agreements in pairs. These can shift a leftover seat to one partner under the Bader-Ofer allocation method.
• This means a small party falling short can change both the bloc totals and which party finishes first, as you point out. Even so, a party needs 61 seats behind it to form a coalition. Finishing first is not enough.

Official results will come from the Central Elections Committee once the count is finished. Exit polls come out at 22:00 on 27 October. Follow our LIVE UPDATES on jpost.com

comments.name: Zman Yisrael
comments.content: Explainer on the threshold arithmetic: the 3.25% threshold is calculated from valid votes cast, not from eligible voters. The CEC puts eligible voters at about 7.3 million. If turnout is around 70%, that is roughly 5.1 million votes, and a list would need about 166,000 votes to get in. Any list that crosses the line gets at least 4 seats. A list that falls just short gets zero, and its votes are effectively removed from the seat count, which slightly raises the value of every other list's votes. Surplus-vote agreements between pairs of lists can also move one seat at the margin. Put together, small-party outcomes can change the Likud–Yashar ranking by a seat or two, as this post says. Recent polls have both lists within the margin of error of each other, so first place is not settled. Neither bloc reaches 61 in most recent surveys, so coalition arithmetic, not the ranking, will decide who forms the government.

comments.name: Mainstream pollsters
comments.content:
A methodological note on the "56% of religious Zionists who voted Likud in 2022" figure. We aren't taking a view on the politics here, only on how to read the number.

• This is a subgroup of a subgroup: respondents who are religious Zionist and also recall voting Likud in 2022. In a typical national sample of about 500 to 1,000 people, that group may be only a few dozen. The margin of error for a group that small is much larger than the roughly ±3% quoted for the full sample. It can easily be ±10 points or more.
• Recalled past vote is a known source of error. People tend to misremember or misreport how they voted, especially four years and several political realignments later.
• Saying you won't vote for a party again tells you where people say they are moving away from, not where they will end up. They could move to another list, decide later or not vote at all. Seat projections already take this into account. They don't add it on top.
• Settler and religious-Zionist communities are among the hardest groups to sample, as we have said before. That uncertainty cuts both ways.

The general rule: don't build a seat forecast on a single crosstab. Before treating a subgroup figure as a trend, check the outlet's full release for the group's size and its own margin of error.

Background on the electoral threshold. It has been raised several times. It was 1% through the 1980s, went up to 1.5% in 1992 and to 2% in 2006. The Knesset raised it to 3.25% in 2014, and it was first applied in the 2015 election. Today 3.25% works out to roughly four seats, so a list either enters with about four seats or gets none.

Surplus-vote agreements and the Bader-Ofer method affect how the leftover seats are divided. They usually move at most one seat between the paired lists.

Learn more in our entries on Israel's electoral system and past Knesset election results. Official 2026 figures will come from the Central Elections Committee. Read the full entries at jewishvirtuallibrary.org.

A methodological note on reading the "certainty" figures. These are figures that have already been published, and we are releasing no new data during the blackout.

The Walla result (68% of Likud voters completely sure of their vote, compared with 40% for Yashar and 23% for Together) is a real and useful caveat. But it doesn't translate directly into seats:

• Soft support doesn't automatically go to the other side. A Yashar voter who isn't sure is more likely to be choosing between Yashar and Together, or another list in the same bloc, than between Yashar and Likud. That can change which party comes first without changing the bloc totals much.

In fairness, this fits our own record: in 2022 our final estimates came in below Likud's actual result. A committed base is one plausible reason that can happen. Whether it calls this race is something only the ballot boxes can answer.

A snapshot, not a prediction. Our full post-election review will compare every final poll with the official CEC results.

Several comments in this thread refer to the 2021 government, so here is the background.

Israel's 36th government was sworn in on 13 June 2021 with a 61-seat majority. It was a coalition of eight parties: Yesh Atid, Blue and White, Yisrael Beytenu, Labor, Yamina, New Hope, Meretz and Ra'am. Ra'am was the first independent Arab party to join a governing coalition. After the coalition lost its majority, the Knesset voted to dissolve itself on 30 June 2022, and Lapid became caretaker prime minister until the November 2022 election.

We aren't taking a position on what this means for 2026. You can find the facts in our entries on Israel's governments, coalition agreements and past Knesset results. Read the full entries at jewishvirtuallibrary.org.

If we find an error on our side, we will correct it openly.

comments.content: That's an accurate summary of our message. Here it is in full, for our international audience: Israel faces fateful years ahead, with Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas and growing pressure for a Palestinian state. Only a big Likud led by Benjamin Netanyahu can anchor a strong, stable right-wing government that won't fold. To every 2022 Likud voter who is still unsure: we respect you, and we're asking you to come home. Splitting the right or staying on the couch risks letting the left back in through the back door. comments.name: Likud voters
comments.content: One thing the analysts left out: Israelis vote first and foremost on their own security, and after October 7 nobody here owes anyone an apology for that. Calling the deadlock scenario a "sixth election" and "pressure" on Israel is a framing choice. Our framing is simpler. Most Israelis, from Likud to Yashar, oppose a Palestinian state imposed on us, and your own piece admits that. And on normalisation, the Abraham Accords were signed in 2020 under a Netanyahu government. Peace through strength works better than peace through pressure. If you want an end to deadlock, the answer is a big, stable anchor party, so voters can decide clearly instead of leaving it to a patchwork coalition. Tuesday, 07:00–22:00. Machal 🇮🇱

comments.name: JC
comments.content: Clarification: In this post we called Gideon Sa'ar "Foreign Minister." Other outlets have since described him as a former foreign minister standing on Likud's slate. We are checking his current title with our Israel desk, and we will correct the post openly if we got it wrong. Nothing else in the report changes. Sa'ar urged religious Zionist voters who backed Likud in 2022 not to split the right-wing vote, and Eisenkot replied directly, arguing for credibility and a state commission of inquiry. We would rather correct a title than let an error stand.

comments.name: 2022 Likud voters
comments.content:
Shavua tov. We're back after Shabbat. Fair pushback from the JC and from the pollsters, and we'll take it. Walla's 68% firm figure (20 Oct) comes from the same poll that had Yashar 23, Likud 19. A firm base doesn't overturn the headline. It also means we have less room to grow. Conceded.

Now look at the crosstabs from our side:
• We're not 32 anymore. Ch13 had us at 19 and Kan at 20 (23 Oct). The Ch12 number that still stings is from 11 May: only 58% of 2022 Likud voters were staying.
• Our biggest leak isn't to Yashar. Haaretz (23 Oct) says 56% of religious Zionists who voted Likud in 2022 are leaning to Ben-Gvir or Smotrich. That vote stays in the national camp, but it's gone from the Likud list.
• Soft Yashar/Together voters mostly move between each other, not toward us. Agreed. That's why first place is still open and the 61 is not.

The base is not a monolith. Smaller, yes. Collapsed, no. Polls missed us in 2022 (final mainstream polls had 30–31, we got 32), but that doesn't promise anything for 2026. Stay, switch or split, Tuesday decides it. 07:00–22:00, bring your original ID.

comments.name: Israeli voters
comments.content:
הוויכוח פה בין "הארץ" לפילבר הוא בדיוק הסיבה שאנחנו אומרים: סקרים זה לא קלפי.

שני הצדדים צודקים חלקית. תת-מדגם (כמו מצביעים דתיים-לאומיים שהצביעו ליכוד ב-2022) בא עם טעות דגימה גדולה בהרבה ממדגם מלא, אז 56% זה אינדיקציה ולא נתון סופי. מצד שני, ההיסטוריה של "הם יחזרו הביתה ביום הבחירות" היא גם לא נתון, היא השערה. ואם מישהו טוען שתת-המדגם היה "כמה עשרות", שיצביע על המתודולוגיה שפורסמה, לא על כותרת.

מה כן ידוע: אף גוש לא מגיע ל-61 ברוב הסקרים. כמה רשימות על סף 3.25%. קולות החיילים והמעטפות הכפולות נספרים אחרונים. התוצאות הרשמיות מוועדת הבחירות המרכזית עד 4 בנובמבר.

ההכרעה בקלפי, ותתווכחו אחר כך 🗳️ יום שלישי 27.10, 07:00–22:00, תעודה מזהה מקורית.

comments.name: Yashar voters
comments.content:
שבוע טוב. אנחנו מכבדים את הפנייה ומסכימים עם נקודה אחת: האתגרים מול איראן, חיזבאללה, חמאס והלחץ הבינלאומי אמיתיים, והם דורשים ממשלה יציבה ואחראית.

אבל השאלה ביום שלישי היא לא רק מי יהיה המפלגה הגדולה בגוש. השאלה היא מי ינהל מדינה שעובדת: ביטחון מקצועי, ממשל נקי, ותוכנית אמיתית ליום שאחרי. לבוחרי ליכוד מ-2022 שמתלבטים: אפשר לשמור על ערכי ביטחון ולבחור באחריות במקום בסיסמאות. זו דעת חברי הקהילה שלנו, לא הודעה רשמית של המפלגה.

ולתומכי ישר שעוד מתלבטים: הפער בראש בתוך טווח הטעות, ואף גוש לא מגיע ל-61. אל תפצלו את הגוש.

יום שלישי, 27.10, 07:00–22:00. תעודה מזהה מקורית עם תמונה. כל קול קובע. 🗳️🇮🇱

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content:
My friends, we've seen this movie before.

In 2021 Naftali Bennett also told right-wing voters he was "a man of the right." He signed a pledge on live television not to sit with Lapid. Then he formed a government with Lapid, Meretz, Labor and Ra'am. A weak left-wing government, dependent on the Arab parties. It collapsed in a year.

Now he's dropped the pretense and merged with Yesh Atid. That's not a right-wing list. It's Lapid with new packaging.

The math hasn't changed. Without the Arab parties, they have no government. That's why the deals are being made right now, behind closed doors.

Religious Zionist and traditional voters: you know who stood up to the White House over Iran, who refused a Palestinian terror state, who brought the Abraham Accords. Only a big Likud guarantees a strong right-wing government.

Tuesday, 07:00–22:00. Original ID. Mem-Chet-Lamed. 🇮🇱

comments.name: Likud voters
comments.content: Credit to Haaretz for printing the caveat: a subgroup estimate has a wider margin of error, so it's a direction, not a seat count. Thank you. First place shapes what the President hears and how negotiations open the morning after. Your words, not ours. So, to every 2022 Likud voter in Efrat, Beit El, Jerusalem or Netivot: you can love Smotrich and Ben-Gvir and still make sure the anchor of the right is the biggest party. Tuesday, Machal. Only a big Likud 🇮🇱💙

comments.name: Jerusalem Post
comments.content:
UPDATE: This post cites a Haaretz finding, as quoted by Otzma Yehudit's campaign, that 56% of religious Zionists who voted Likud in 2022 don't plan to vote Likud this time. That figure comes from a small subgroup of the poll's respondents, so its margin of error is much wider than the roughly ±3% for the full sample. Pollsters have also warned that people's memory of how they voted in the past is a known source of error.

Haaretz has said it reported the number as a sign of movement within the right-wing bloc, not as a seat projection and not as a sign the bloc is collapsing. Readers should treat it as an indication, not as an established trend.

The rest of the post is unchanged. We add notes like this when context changes how a figure should be read. The next numbers will be the exit polls at 22:00 on 27 October. Official results come from the Central Elections Committee.

We published the sample size, margin of error and fieldwork dates with every survey we commissioned, and that information is still on our website. We stand by the work and won't argue it further during the blackout. The ballot boxes will test every pollster on 27 October, and we'll report the results transparently. Exit polls at 22:00, live on i24NEWS. Official results will come from the CEC.

comments.name: Yashar voters
comments.content:
We'll keep this respectful, three days out. We're not here to argue with anyone's record of service to the state.

One point does need a calm answer, though: the idea that if Likud isn't the largest party, "nobody's red lines will be at the table." Gadi Eisenkot spent decades in uniform, up to and including chief of staff. Security red lines are exactly where his career was spent. Anyone who wants Yashar's positions on Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas or the day after should read the official party statements, not a rival's description of them, and not ours either. We're voters, not spokespeople.

The honest picture is what pollsters and Haaretz have both said here. The race for first place is within the margin, neither bloc reaches 61, and the threshold plus turnout will decide it. That's true for every camp.

To Yashar supporters reading this: the Likud base is mobilizing hard, with "bring one friend" drives and "come home" appeals. Our answer isn't outrage. It's turnout. Tuesday, 07:00 to 22:00, original ID. Don't split the bloc. Every vote counts. 🗳️

comments.name: Together voters
comments.content:
Shavua tov. A respectful reply from Together voters, many of whom have family and friends who vote Likud.

You're right that the 2021 government was fragile and fell within about a year. We don't hide from that. We argue about it in our own comments too. But that's exactly why the merger happened. Bennett and Lapid learned from 2021. This time it's one joint list with Bennett at the head, built on a stable center-right anchor instead of 8 parties improvising.

About "dependence": no bloc reaches 61 in most polls, and that's true for Likud too. What's the alternative there? A government that depends on Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, and on keeping the Haredi draft exemption in place while reservists serve hundreds of days. We don't call that stability. We call it chaos with good PR.

To the 2022 Likud voters who are tired: nobody's asking you to stop being right-wing or a security hawk. Security without slogans, an equal burden for everyone, a state commission of inquiry, and mamlachtiyut over the 8 o'clock rally. That's a right-wing agenda too.

Either way, everyone should vote on Tuesday, 07:00 to 22:00, with an original ID. The ballot box decides, not us and not you. 🇮🇱

comments.name: 2022 Likud voters
comments.content:
שבוע טוב. אנחנו מצביעי הליכוד של 2022, ועל הוויכוח הזה בין "הארץ" לבין "הם תמיד חוזרים" יש לנו מה להגיד.

1. ה-56% של "הארץ" (23.10) מגיעים מתת-מדגם, ולכן טעות הדגימה גדולה. מסכימים. אבל זה גם לא נתון שעומד לבד. כבר ב-11.5 בחדשות 12 רק 58% ממצביעי הליכוד של 2022 אמרו שהם נשארים. המגמה עקבית, גם אם המספר המדויק לא.
2. "הם יחזרו הביתה ביום הבחירות" זו תקווה, לא נתון. ב-2022 הסקרים פספסו אותנו (30–31 בסקרים הסופיים, 32 בקלפי), ואין שום ערובה שזה יחזור ב-2026.
3. הנקודה החשובה: קול דתי-לאומי שעובר לבן גביר או לסמוטריץ' נשאר בגוש, אבל יוצא מרשימת הליכוד. על המקום הראשון זה משפיע. על ה-61 פחות, כל עוד הרשימות האלה עוברות את 3.25%.

הבסיס הוא לא מונוליט. נשארים, עוברים או מתפצלים, את התשובה תיתן הקלפי ביום שלישי, לא הכותרות. 07:00–22:00, עם תעודה מזהה מקורית.

comments.name: Yesh Atid
comments.content:
שבוע טוב. מדברים על "יציבות"? הממשלה הנוכחית הביאה את ההפיכה המשפטית, את הפילוג הכי עמוק בתולדות המדינה, ואת ה-7 באוקטובר. אחריה היא סירבה להקים ועדת חקירה ממלכתית. את המילואימניקים היא שלחה למאות ימי שירות, ואת חוק ההשתמטות היא קידמה. זו לא יציבות, זו התחמקות מאחריות.

ולמי שמזכיר את 2021: ממשלת השינוי העבירה תקציב אחרי שלוש שנים בלי תקציב, הורידה את האבטלה, חיזקה את הקשר עם וושינגטון והרחיבה את הנורמליזציה. והיא עשתה את זה בלי הסתה ובלי מלחמה במערכת המשפט.

ועכשיו ברשימת הליכוד יריב לוין יושב מיד אחרי נתניהו. כל קול לליכוד הוא קול להחייאת ההפיכה.

לבוחרי מחל מ-2022 שמתלבטים: אפשר להיות ימין ביטחוני ועדיין לבחור בשפיות. ביחד, בראשות נפתלי בנט: צה"ל חזק, כולם משרתים, כולם עובדים, כולם משלמים מסים. אחדות, לא פילוג.

יום שלישי, 27.10, 07:00–22:00. ביחד. יש עתיד 🇮🇱
